rationale: bugs_open/330 (090 CONFIRMED) is the `?` marker's motivating case and this is its fix. Both tool BUILD steps wire `related_pages` to `input_data.spec.related_pages` (migration 211), but most add_tool specs omit the key; a declared path that resolves to nothing does not stop the resolver, so the field falls through to the whole-tree search, which finds only `load_brand_context.specs.tools.suggestions[N].related_pages` and takes suggestions[0]'s. On webdesign.co.uk that cross-linked NINE tools to the SAME TWO pages - correct for exactly one tool (the A/B Test Significance Calculator, which IS suggestions[0]), wrong for the other eight. 32 items, 0 reached live content (22 failed, 6 wont_fix, 2 triaged, 2 unresolved), so the cost so far is wasted writer work and a polluted queue. The fix converts both wires to the `?` OPTIONAL-EXPLICIT marker (live on v1.0.1321): the suggestion's own path or ABSENCE, never the search. WHY NOT THE ALTERNATIVES, both of which this lane considered on the record: a PLAIN wire is what is deployed today and its miss IS the bug; 512's `input_fields` shape (which correctly fixed tool-generator/`reason`) would lose the legitimate case, because unlike `reason` there IS a path we want when the spec carries it. The lane's own ledger line for this pair - 'refusal is the DESIRED outcome, so it needs a recorded decision, not a wire' - was written before the marker was live and is superseded: the wire is how the refusal gets declared. ABSENCE-SAFETY READ AT THE CONSUMER, first-hand, not assumed: both actions reach one helper (relatedPagesFromInputs, create_tool_cross_link_items.go:443, called from create_tool_component_action.go:527 and deploy_tool_action.go:271,548); with the field absent GetRaw is nil and it re-reads the same declared path directly, also nil, so absence propagates with nothing reaching for a search; and absence is INSTRUMENTED rather than tolerated (create_tool_cross_link_items.go:142-151 logs at info and records a counted skip `no_related_pages` with the comment 'Not a defect: a suggestion may legitimately name no related pages'), which is exactly the downstream confirmation RFC_029 Sec 10.15's adoption gate requires and which is recorded in optional_explicit_wire_acks.json in this same commit. THE FILE IS _HOLD AND THE ORDERING CONDITION IS NOT A ROLL - this is the part I most want reviewed. The binary precondition is already met. It is held because applying it CONSUMES the demand control that migration 512's verification depends on: 512's stated test is 'reason 0 WHILE related_pages KEEPS FIRING (if both go quiet the instrument died and the zero means nothing)', and 512 is applied but unverified. Measured 2026-08-21: tool-generator runs since 512's boundary = 0 over 18 h, so today's quiet on BOTH classes is no demand, not no defect. Apply conditions and the two queries are in the file header; after applying, 330's own verification needs fresh tool-generator demand and its instrument-alive control must come from another agent's live class (bdl/commit_sha), because this file removes the local one.

plan.risks: Applying this before 512 is verified would silence both tool-generator classes at once and make 512 permanently unverifiable - which is why the file is _HOLD with that as its stated condition, and the whole reason it is not simply applied today. The second step (tool-deployer) has no logged rows, so its conversion is prophylactic: if some caller of deploy_tool_to_site were relying on the searched value, this removes it silently - I judge that unlikely to the point of being the desired outcome (the searched value is another tool's pages by construction), but it is the one behaviour change here with no instrument behind it. After apply, 330's verification needs fresh tool-generator demand (~16 runs/24h historically, but 0 in the last 18 h) and its instrument-alive control must come from another agent's class. This does not close 330's general half - an unmarked wired-but-empty field anywhere else still falls through - which stays candidate 2, gated on the 269-pair unsampled remainder.
